corrections.problem: The note never opens the mod's server-side peer bookkeeping, and that is where C6 and vehicles actually collide. `LogicalPeerCutoverRunner.DrainMotion` (network/mod/ComfyNetworkSense/Core/Services/LogicalPeerCutoverRunner.cs:109-150) writes `matched.Peer.m_refPos` directly from the C6 motion snapshot XYZ (:131-134). In vanilla that field is only ever set from `RPC_ServerSyncedPlayerData` (DECOMP/ZNet.cs:1386-1393), a direct ZRpc that native-zero suppresses. `peer.m_refPos` is the input to `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS(peer.m_peer.m_refPos, peer.m_peer.m_uid)` (ZDOMan.cs:605), `ZDOPeer.ShouldSend` (ZDOMan.cs:40), the per-peer sync list (ZDOMan.cs:897) and `ZoneSystem.CreateGhostZones(peer.GetRefPos())` (ZoneSystem.cs:953). So the note's fork C ('how does a rider's transform travel') is not a rendering choice — it silently decides the server's entire area-of-interest for that peer.
corrections.correction: Rewrite fork C with a hard constraint: every attached player must keep publishing a world-space position on the C6 frame, or `DrainMotion` must be taught to resolve the parent before writing `m_refPos`. Price the two options accordingly — C2 ('let attached players fall back to native ZSyncTransform') stops refPos updates for an entire voyage, so the server stops sending ZDOs and starts releasing ownership around the boarding point while the boat sails into unloaded ocean; C1 ('parent-relative pose in the frame') writes relative coordinates into `m_refPos`, teleporting the peer's AoI to near-origin. Neither failure produces an error.

corrections.problem: E1, E3 (cart leg) and E4 all presuppose a boat, cart, or tamed mount exists in the AM4 world, and the lab has no way to create one. `spawn` is registered `isCheat: true` (Terminal.cs:1206 + the trailing flags line, which carries the `ZNetScene.instance.GetPrefabNames()` options fetcher), as is `tame` (Terminal.cs:1480-1483). The gate is absolute: `IsCheatsEnabled()` returns `ZNet.instance.IsServer()` (Terminal.cs:2232-2243) and `IsValid` short-circuits on `!IsCheat || context.IsCheatsEnabled()` (Terminal.cs:236). On a client attached to a dedicated server `IsServer()` is false, so no cheat command runs regardless of admin status — the repo already knows this and worked around it for exactly one command (ComfyNetworkSense.cs:999-1001: "the vanilla 'god'/'fly' console commands are cheat-gated on a dedicated-server client"). `-console` IS passed at launch (Invoke-NativeValheimClient.ps1:647), which makes this failure look surprising in the moment. E1's parenthetical "(spawn it on A)" is therefore not a step, it is the unbudgeted prerequisite. Hand-building is not free either: a Karve needs 80 bronze nails, a Cart needs 10, a tamed Lox needs Plains plus taming time. Evidence that something saddleable is already near the test area exists but is weak and probably wild — `Setting saddle:False` (Tameable.cs:386) appears in omen bepinex.log across full32/full34/full43/c8twoclient16/portalgate14, one line each; no Karve/VikingShip/Cart/Raft string appears anywhere under fieldlab/runs or fieldlab/evidence.
corrections.correction: Make world seeding an explicit, first, separately-scheduled item: stand up a local non-dedicated host on the ComfyEra16 save (where `IsCheatsEnabled()` is true), `spawn Karve`/`spawn Cart`/`spawn Lox`+`tame` at fixed coordinates near the existing test origin (2211,80,-69) and the Plains target (3250,80,2250), then redeploy the .db/.fwl to AM4 and re-baseline `Get-Am4SaveFingerprint` (Invoke-NativeValheimCutoverScenario.ps1:217-276 — `portals`/`spawned`/`targets`/`locations` are compared exact, so the before-baseline must be recaptured after seeding). Separately: run the whole vanilla-oracle half of section 6 (does `Ship.m_players` populate for a remote, what does `s_user` actually contain, does the attach channel emit, does a cart pull churn ownership) on that same local-host + one-client pair. It is cheat-enabled, needs no manifest, no Gateway, no poison, and no AM4 time.

corrections.problem: E4 is not runnable on this harness at any cost, because there is no verb that can put a player on a vehicle and no verb that can move a player in a way that respects one. The action-kind set is closed and re-validated in-process — anything else returns `manifest_action_kind_invalid` (NativeCutoverScenarioController.cs:202-278). The only two interaction verbs are `pickup_nearest`, hard-typed to `AccessTools.TypeByName("Pickable")` and rejecting everything else with `pickable_type_unavailable`/`pickable_not_found` (:645-690), and `ownership_target`, which calls `ZNetView.ClaimOwnership()` on the nearest GameObject whose *name* contains a tag that must start with `cutover-<runid>` (:883-911, SafeTargetTag at :1123-1126) — no world object is ever named that, and the accepted composition does not use it. There is no board, use, helm, hitch, mount, sit, or steer verb. Worse, the two movement verbs are transform teleports, not locomotion: `move` does `((Component)Player.m_localPlayer).transform.position = target` with `target.y = _origin.y` (:337-343), and `motion_drive` does the identical thing (LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:906-918). `_origin`/`probe.Origin` are captured in absolute world space at action start. So a "passenger on the deck" driven by `move` is pinned to a fixed world line and a fixed Y while the hull translates and pitches underneath — the harness's own writes would dominate the exact quantity E4 wants to measure (observer-side rider-to-deck offset), and would also fight `Character`'s deck-stick `m_body.position` write. The note's claim that E4 "needs no new scenario kind... everything else is existing machinery" is false in both halves.
corrections.correction: Drop E4 from the cheap tier. If the rider-separation question survives E2 (i.e. `m_characterParentSync` is true on the Player prefab), it requires new mod code: at minimum a `vehicle_board`/`vehicle_helm` action kind driving `ShipControlls.Interact`, plus a passenger verb that does NOT write `transform.position` (or that writes parent-relative), plus a new observer-side measurement that samples rider world position against the parent ZDO's position per frame. That is a slice of work, not an experiment. In the interim the same question is answerable for free on the local-host + one-client pair with no Lumberjacks at all: it establishes the vanilla baseline offset, which you need anyway before an A/B means anything.

corrections.correction: H5's conclusion survives — the three vehicle SetOwner calls are not blocked — but the reason is the predicate, not a missing hook. `ShouldBlockRelease` (:205-216) requires `ReleaseScopeDepth > 0`, and `ReleaseScopeDepth` is incremented in exactly one place: the prefix on `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (:1125-1127). So the guard is scoped exclusively to the AoI sweep, and Ship.cs:696 / Sadle.cs:349 / Vagon.cs:141 pass through because they fire outside that scope, not because they are unhookable. This cuts in the note's favour and should be corrected before the note is planned against: the universal interception point vehicles need already exists and is already proven. C10a needs a wider predicate (scope condition + target selection), not a new seam. That materially reduces the cost of fork A3 as sized in §4.A.

corrections.problem: An entire family is absent, and vanilla itself classifies it alongside ships: fishing. `ZDOMan.ConvertOwnerships` (DECOMP/ZDOMan.cs:1305-1321) converts `s_zdoidUser`→`s_user` and `s_zdoidRodOwner`→`s_rodOwner` in one loop, logged as 'Converting Ships & Fishing-rods ownership' (:365). `FishingFloat` writes `ZDOVars.s_rodOwner` (FishingFloat.cs:87) — a fifth identity space beyond the three fork D enumerates — and resolves it via `ZNet.instance.GetPlayerList()` matched on `m_characterID.UserID` then `ZNetScene.FindInstance` (:100-120), the same peer-list dependency that breaks `Sadle.CalculateHaveValidUser`. `Fish` is pulled continuously toward the float by the fish ZDO's owner (`Utils.Pull`, Fish.cs:403-410) — a cross-ZDO continuous physics coupling with exactly the vehicle shape — and registers `RequestPickup`/`Pickup` with a targeted unicast `InvokeRPC(uid, "Pickup")` (:222-223, :303).
corrections.correction: Add fishing as a family-1 member and note that its failure mode is not the note's 'silent no-op': `FishingFloat.FixedUpdate` calls `m_nview.Destroy()` when the owner cannot be resolved (:136-145). The same missing-peer-list root cause is silent for mounts and destructive for fishing floats — that difference should drive test ordering.

corrections.correction: State family 1 as {Ship, ShipControlls, Sadle, Vagon, Catapult, SiegeMachine, ShipConstructor, ShipEffects, Leviathan} and the method count as 19, not 16. corrections.problem: Even given a boat and a boarding verb, E4's stated A/B ("C6 authority ON and OFF") cannot be run inside the native-zero composition. The cutover flags are per-run request fields, not runtime toggles (NativeAutotestRequest.cs:30-38, set once at load from the file the launcher writes), so ON/OFF is two full runs rather than an A/B — that alone doubles the cost. More decisively, the mod refuses the combination: `SteamFreeColdJoin` with `!MotionAuthorityCutover` is rejected as `steam_free_request_cutover_prerequisites_invalid` (NativeAutotestRequest.cs:141-149). So the OFF cell cannot be a Steam-free cold-join run. Whatever composition you use for OFF differs from the ON cell in join path, world-descriptor handling, and peer bootstrap, which is precisely the kind of cross-composition difference that has produced calibration misses in this lane before.
corrections.correction: State the OFF cell's composition explicitly and accept that it is a vanilla-transport baseline, not a matched control. Or make the ON/OFF distinction narrower and legal — e.g. an authority-scope flag that excludes ZDOs with a resolved `SyncTransform` connection — so both cells stay inside the same accepted native-zero composition. That is a design decision for the slice, not something to discover at run time.

corrections.angle: Harness feasibility and experimental discrimination: can the two-client AM4 manifest-driven composition actually run E1-E5, and would the results discriminate anything?
corrections.problem: E1 names an instrument that cannot carry the signal. It predicts "`LogicalPeerCutoverRunner._suppressedInvokes` climbs (sampled log lines at counts 1-4 and powers of two)". But `TryHandleInvoke` increments that single counter for *every* suppressed `ZRpc.Invoke` on a logical peer (LogicalPeerCutoverRunner.cs:339), and `ZDOMan.SendZDOToPeers2` invokes `ZDOData` on a 0.05s timer (ZDOMan.cs:565-571, 787) — 20 Hz, continuously, plus NetTime and the rest. Over a 30-minute manual session that is roughly 36,000 increments; the power-of-two sampler fires at 16384 and then not again until 32768, i.e. once in a fourteen-minute stretch. The method name is only emitted on those samples (:367-371). You would watch a number go up and be unable to attribute a single increment to the moment someone pressed Use on a boat. The note also undersells its own strongest instrument: the run-level discriminator is the *server-side* poison ledger, because inbound `RPC_RoutedRPC` calls `NativeNetworkLedger.Observe("routed_rpc_receive", "inbound", "RoutedRPC")` (NativeNetworkPatches.cs:204-206). Either the vehicle RPC never leaves the client (no server row, silent swallow, H1 confirmed) or it lands on the server and trips poison (H1 refuted, run aborts loudly). That fork is clean, already collected as `native-network-use.jsonl`, and needs no sampling at all.
corrections.correction: Rewrite E1's success criteria around the server-side `native-network-use.jsonl` trip/no-trip fork. If per-method attribution on the client is wanted (and it is, to prove *which* method was swallowed), add a small always-log carve-out in `TryHandleInvoke` for methods outside a known-noisy set (`ZDOData`, `NetTime`, `PlayerPos`), or a per-method counter dictionary — that is a two-line change but it is a change, so E1 stops being "no code".

corrections.angle: Harness feasibility and experimental discrimination: can the two-client AM4 manifest-driven composition actually run E1-E5, and would the results discriminate anything?
corrections.problem: E4's stated motion windows exceed what the mod will accept, and the composition is close to its action ceiling. The generator advertises `-MotionDurationSeconds` 4..120 and `-MotionDistanceMeters` 2..200 (New-NativeValheimCutoverScenario.ps1:30-37), but the in-process validator rejects any motion probe with `duration_seconds` outside 2..20 or `distance_meters` above 24 (NativeCutoverScenarioController.cs:263-270) — the manifest is refused wholesale with `manifest_motion_probe_invalid`, not clamped. A "straight run and a turn" on a longship is minutes and hundreds of metres; you get 20 seconds and 24 metres. Separately, the manifest cap is `MaxActions = 64` checked before the per-client filter (:27, :184-187), and the accepted C8 composition already uses 49 actions across both clients. Fifteen slots remain, shared, and a two-client board/helm/observe/settle cell burns them fast.
corrections.correction: Note the generator/validator range mismatch as a standing bug worth fixing regardless (the generator should not be able to emit a manifest the mod always rejects). For vehicle work, plan a separate profile rather than extending `c8` — and size the action budget before designing the choreography, not after.

corrections.angle: Harness feasibility and experimental discrimination: can the two-client AM4 manifest-driven composition actually run E1-E5, and would the results discriminate anything?
corrections.problem: E3 is neither free nor unambiguous. The finding that `TelemetryCoordinator.RecordOwnershipChurn` exists (TelemetryCoordinator.cs:439-444) with zero callers is correct and genuinely useful — but the class exposes no static accessor a Harmony patch can reach (the only `Instance` reference in the file is `ComfyNetworkSense.Instance.Config.Reload()` at :329), so the postfix needs a static hook wired the way the other runners do it. And `ownership-churn.jsonl` is not in the orchestrator's evidence pull: the collected set for the accepted run (fieldlab/runs/native-valheim/native-20260731-c8-full44/omen/) is 18 files and does not include it, so the orchestrator needs a collection change too. Beyond cost, there is a design ambiguity the note does not resolve: measured on the *cutover* composition, `ZDO.SetOwner` churn is Lumberjacks' behaviour (the C3 journal and world/zone cutover are already in the ownership path), not vanilla's — so it cannot answer "is cart churn folklore" about vanilla. And the cart leg is unscriptable anyway: hitching a cart needs `Vagon.Interact`, which `pickup_nearest` cannot reach.
corrections.correction: Split E3 in two. The vanilla-baseline half belongs on the local-host + one-client pair with the mod in observe-only mode — cheap, cheat-enabled, and it answers the `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` hysteresis question the note actually cares about. The cutover half is a real instrumentation task: static hook, Harmony postfix on `ZDO.SetOwner` recording (prefab, old_owner, new_owner, callsite), plus an orchestrator collection entry. Say which side of the boundary each cell runs on.

corrections.correction: `_remote` has exactly two insertion sites, `LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:680` (`_remote[key] = updated;`) and `:1352` (`_remote[snapshot.ZdoUserId + ":" + snapshot.ZdoId] = remote;`). Both key purely on the motion frame's own ZDO identity. The only admission filter on the drain path is `if (!_remoteDescriptors.ContainsKey(key)) { ... continue; }` at `:650`. Nothing anywhere in that path consults attach state, `m_attached`, a parent connection, or `GetRelativePosition`. A ridden or deck-standing remote player is an ordinary remote player and is admitted normally. H3's remaining uncertainty therefore collapses to a single prefab flag — E2's `m_characterParentSync` answer — which strengthens the note's own sequencing argument for running E2 first.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: C4's one-shot lease shape does not express a continuous control claim; naively reusing it means one lease validation per rudder frame
hazards.why: C4 attaches a lease epoch to a single mutating action and the server validates before mutating. `Ship.ApplyControlls` (Ship.cs:201-225) emits an absolute rudder value up to 5x/second for as long as the pilot holds the key, plus edge-triggered throttle steps. A per-action lease check turns into a per-frame check on a hot path, and — worse — the lease *epoch* has no natural place to ride in an absolute-value stream where old frames must be dropped, not rejected. The vehicle lease needs a held-lease-with-expiry shape (grant, heartbeat, revoke) that C4 has not proven, plus a sequence number the vanilla protocol does not have.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: Vanilla's throttle is a relative state machine with no idempotency, so any retransmit/reorder/loss silently desynchronises ship speed
hazards.why: RPC_Forward/RPC_Backward (Ship.cs:257-297) step the enum rather than setting it: Stop→Slow→Half→Full. Over a lossy or reordered UDP lane a dropped Forward leaves the owner one notch behind the pilot's belief forever (the pilot has no local m_speed prediction — it reads `s_forward` back). If Lumberjacks carries these as-is it inherits a protocol that was only ever safe over ordered, reliable Steam channels. The fix (send the absolute Speed enum) is a wire-contract change that must be decided in C10a design, not discovered in test.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: Nothing in vanilla authorizes ship movement, so the lease is a genuine new security boundary and will change observable behaviour
hazards.why: RPC_Rudder/RPC_Stop/RPC_Forward/RPC_Backward (Ship.cs:242-297) have no IsOwner check, no sender-vs-s_user check, and RPC_RequestRespons (ShipControlls.cs:117) starts doodad control on the receiver unconditionally. hazards.why: ZSyncTransform.OwnerSync writes `ZDOExtraData.ConnectionType.SyncTransform` → ship ZDOID, plus s_relPos/s_relRot/s_vel in ship space (ZSyncTransform.cs:183-214), and SyncPosition resolves and steps the PARENT before placing the child (line 276-345). C6's canonical motion frame carries world position/rotation/velocity for a player. A player standing on a moving deck has a world position that is only meaningful jointly with the ship's pose at the same instant — sending world-space frames for a passenger on a ship owned by a third peer reintroduces exactly the rubber-banding C6 eliminated for ground movement. The motion frame likely needs an optional parent-ZDO + relative-frame variant, and the ordering guarantee (parent resolved first) has to be preserved.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: Ownership migrates on a 2s tick from two independent tickers, and RPCs are addressed to the owner at send time — a lease-holder can be validated against a stale owner
hazards.why: `ZNetView.InvokeRPC` resolves the target from `m_zdo.GetOwner()` at send (ZNetView.cs:326-329); `Ship.UpdateOwner` (client, 2s) and `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` (server, 2s) can both move ownership between send and receive. Vanilla tolerates this by silently dropping the input. A fail-closed Lumberjacks validator will instead reject, and if the lease is keyed to the simulating peer rather than to the vehicle, a routine 2s handoff produces a burst of lease-mismatch rejections that look like an attack. The lease must be vehicle-scoped and survive owner migration, or the migration itself must be lease-mediated.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: Two identity spaces collide in one grant path, and neither matches the Lumberjacks logical-peer id
hazards.why: `s_user` for ships holds `Player.GetPlayerID()` — a persistent profile UID generated client-side (`Utils.GenerateUID()`, PlayerProfile.cs:120) and therefore trivially spoofable and not authenticated by the handshake; `Sadle` stores `GetZDOID().UserID` instead (Sadle.cs:224); ZDO ownership uses the session/peer id. C4's lease is keyed to an *authenticated logical-peer id*. Mapping any of these onto that id is not mechanical: the profile UID is exactly the wrong thing to trust, and RPC_ReleaseControl authorizes on the payload rather than the sender (ShipControlls.cs:111), which is a free eviction primitive today.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: On a headless dedicated server no peer necessarily simulates a ship, and the server cannot become the fallback simulator without new work
hazards.why: `Ship.UpdateOwner` early-returns when `Player.m_localPlayer == null`, so the dedicated host never participates in ship ownership handoff. The server's own reference position is never set (every `SetReferencePosition` caller is local-player driven: Game.cs:459/488/510/513, Player.cs:644/1502, Tracker.cs, Valkyrie.cs), so its active area — and therefore its `ReleaseNearbyZDOS` seize window — sits at the world origin. If Lumberjacks moves vehicle simulation server-side (the natural fail-closed design), that is a genuinely new capability: the server must instantiate, own and step Ship rigidbodies in zones nobody has claimed, with the water/Heightmap dependencies (`Floating.GetWaterLevel`, `Heightmap.ForceGenerateAll` at Ship.cs:156) those forces need.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: Client-side rudder prediction has a hard 1s reconciliation hold that will read as a bug under a new transport
hazards.why: Ship.UpdateControlls (Ship.cs:576-579) refuses to accept the authoritative `s_rudder` for 1 full second after the local peer's last send. Under the current native lane the round trip hides inside that window. If a Lumberjacks lease adds validation latency or a rejection, the pilot sees their predicted rudder held for up to a second and then snap — indistinguishable from lag in a C9-style motion-quality capture unless the reconciliation policy is deliberately re-specified alongside the transport.

hazards.lens: Ship control and ownership (Valheim `Ship` / `ShipControlls`) — vanilla source of truth for C10a vehicle admission
hazards.hazard: `Ship.Rudder(float)` is a trap for a mechanical port
hazards.why: Ship.cs:237-240 reads `m_nview.Invoke("Rudder", rudder)`, which is `MonoBehaviour.Invoke(methodName, delay)` — ZNetView defines no such method (ZNetView.cs only defines Register/InvokeRPC). It is unreferenced dead code across the whole decomp. An agent enumerating 'ship RPC surface' by method name will admit a phantom `Rudder` entry point and may wire real behaviour to it.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: C6 motion authority silently disables the rider's attach-to-mount glue on every observer
hazards.why: On a remote observer the rider's parent-relative placement is produced inside ZSyncTransform.ClientSync -> SyncPosition (ZSyncTransform.cs:276-345), reached only from CustomFixedUpdate. MotionAuthorityTransformPatch prefixes exactly that method and returns false for any ZDO Lumberjacks tracks (LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:1369). A ridden player IS tracked. So the moment the C6 lane owns a rider, the attach-joint snap stops running and the rider is placed by absolute Lumberjacks motion frames while the mount underneath is still placed by native ZDO interpolation. Two independent placement lanes for two rigidly-coupled bodies means guaranteed visible separation, worst at speed and on turns. This is not a tuning problem — the coupling code is simply not executing.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Mount ownership and steering intent replicate on different channels with no epoch tying them together
hazards.why: Sadle.cs:346-349 writes s_user (DataRevision) and SetOwner (OwnerRevision) as two independent facts, and tells the client it has control BEFORE issuing the ownership change. C4's lease proved a server-originated epoch on a one-shot action. A mount lease must instead bind (a) rider identity, (b) simulation rights, and (c) a continuous validity window into one epoch, and must survive the entire ride. There is no vanilla mechanism to copy here — the vanilla design just assumes the two revisions converge.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Making the server the mount's ZDO owner converts a zero-byte control loop into a per-input-frame wire message
hazards.why: Sadle.ApplyControlls fires every input frame (Sadle.cs:268 via PlayerController.cs:160/164) and ZRoutedRpc short-circuits it locally today because the rider owns the ZDO (ZRoutedRpc.cs:130). Any Lumberjacks design that keeps mount authority server-side turns that into ~60 msg/s per rider with no vanilla rate limiting, batching, or sequencing. There is also no ack, no sequence number, and RPC_Controls has sticky-state semantics (Sadle.cs:279-298) that are order-sensitive — a dropped or reordered Speed transition leaves the mount stuck walking or turning.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: BaseAI/MonsterAI simulation rights are inseparable from ZDO ownership
hazards.why: BaseAI.UpdateAI hard-returns on non-owners (BaseAI.cs:309) and MonsterAI hands its whole tick to the saddle (MonsterAI.cs:356). You cannot split 'the server validates control' from 'the rider simulates the creature' without either replacing the AI tick gate or accepting that the rider's client remains the physics authority for a non-player entity — which is exactly the thing C6 removed for players. Whichever way this goes, the ownership handoff must not stall the AI tick: a mid-transfer window where NEITHER machine owns the ZDO stops the creature dead (the C8 audit already flags AI handoff stalls as a needed verification cell).

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: HaveRider() is computed from a peer-scoped list and is already wrong on bystander clients in vanilla
hazards.why: ZNet.GetAllCharacterZDOS (ZNet.cs:1847-1867) returns the local character plus directly-connected peers' characters. A client on a dedicated server sees only its own. So Sadle.CalculateHaveValidUser (Sadle.cs:363-379) yields false on every non-rider client, silently changing mount run speed, slide angle and animation there (Character.cs:1084/1493/3603). Lumberjacks replaces the peer/handshake layer, and the whole thing hangs off the direct (non-routed) ZRpc 'CharacterID' message (ZNet.cs:1806-1825). If that mapping is not carried, the SERVER also stops being able to evaluate rider validity — which is the one place that check has to work if the lease is server-issued.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Nothing clears s_user on disconnect, death, or unload; recovery depends on a fragile derived check
hazards.why: Exhaustive grep shows s_user is written only at Sadle.cs:346 and Sadle.cs:385. Rider disconnect and rider death both leave it populated (Player.OnDeath has no release path; Player.cs:745 gates the release path behind !IsDead()). Vanilla un-sticks only because CalculateHaveValidUser fails the 10 m distance test or finds no matching character ZDO. If Lumberjacks changes how the rider's character ZDO is registered or how positions are sourced, that implicit recovery can invert: a mount permanently reporting a valid user, refusing every RequestControl and refusing saddle removal (Sadle.cs:331-337 requires !HaveValidUser).

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Abandoned mount reclaim depends entirely on the generic 2 s server sweep, which only touches Persistent ZDOs
hazards.why: ZDOMan.RemovePeer does nothing mount-specific (ZDOMan.cs:498-509); recovery is ReleaseNearbyZDOS (ZDOMan.cs:623-648), server-only, every 2 s, filtered by `if (!tempNearObject.Persistent) continue`. If a Lumberjacks ownership lane replaces or bypasses that sweep, a mount whose rider crashed mid-ride stays owned by a dead session and stops being simulated by anyone. The 2 s worst case also means a mid-ride disconnect leaves a rider-shaped hole where the creature is frozen for up to two seconds before another client takes over — visible to everyone nearby.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: The rider's position is resolved by string bone-name lookup at presentation time, not by any transform you control
hazards.why: The remote path does Utils.FindChild(mountGO.transform, attachJointName) and snaps to that child's world position (ZSyncTransform.cs:301-306), and it force-ticks the mount's ZSyncTransform first (line 287) so the parent is current in the same frame. Any Lumberjacks rider representation must reproduce both the name-keyed resolution AND that intra-frame ordering. Re-implementing rider placement as an absolute position stream loses the ordering guarantee even if the numbers are right — you'd be one frame stale against the mount's own update, every frame.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Rider rotation is forced to the mount's rotation, so a rider motion frame carrying its own rotation is wrong by construction
hazards.why: Player.GetRelativePosition returns relativeRot = Quaternion.identity for a Character parent (Player.cs:6713-6714), and SyncPosition slerps toward parentRot * relRot then sets usedLocalRotation = true, suppressing the absolute-rotation branch (ZSyncTransform.cs:330-337). C6's motion frames are the sole remote source of player rotation. While mounted, that authority is supposed to be delegated to the mount's rotation, not asserted by the rider — the lane needs an explicit 'attached, rotation deferred' state or riders will visibly counter-rotate against their mounts.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: RPC_RequestRespons acts on Player.m_localPlayer with no correlation to the request
hazards.why: Sadle.cs:390-408 mounts the local player on any granted response that reaches this client, with no check that this client sent the RequestControl and no request/response id. Vanilla is protected only by the fact that the grant is unicast to `sender`. Lumberjacks routing must preserve strict unicast for RequestRespons; any broadcast or mis-fanout (the ADR-0013 multicast work is explicitly in flight and unproven) would mount uninvolved players onto creatures they never touched.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Mount control shares the ZDO field name and the RPC names with ships
hazards.why: Sadle and ShipControlls both register RequestControl / ReleaseControl / RequestRespons and both use ZDOVars.s_user — same hashes, different ZDOs. A lease lane keyed on method-name hash rather than on (ZDO, prefab kind) will conflate the two, even though their ownership semantics differ (Sadle forces SetOwner, ShipControlls does not). Poison guards and contract tests must be per-target-ZDO, not per-RPC-name.

hazards.lens: Mounts (saddle / tamed creature) — Sadle, Tameable, MonsterAI/BaseAI, Character/Player attach, ZSyncTransform relative sync
hazards.hazard: Saddle add/remove/drop are separate ZDO+broadcast facts that can desync from the ride state
hazards.why: s_haveSaddleHash plus an Everybody 'SetSaddle' RPC (Tameable.cs:328-344) toggles the saddle GameObject active, and Sadle.Awake registers its RPCs on the creature's ZNetView regardless. If SetSaddle deactivates the saddle object while a rider is attached — or if the Everybody broadcast is lost on one client — that client's mount renders saddle-less with a floating rider, and Sadle.FixedUpdate stops running there (UpdateRiding checks base.isActiveAndEnabled at Sadle.cs:132).

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: There is no server-side cart simulator to move authority to
hazards.why: The joint, the Rigidbody integration, and the pulling forces exist only on the cart's owning CLIENT (Vagon.cs:181-189, 252-285). A dedicated server never instantiates the cart because `ZNet.GetReferencePosition()` is never set away from origin on a headless node (ZNetScene.cs:358-366; every SetReferencePosition call site is client-side). So a server-issued lease can say who may drive the cart, but the server cannot itself hold or validate the resulting motion the way C6 validates player motion frames. Either the design accepts client-authoritative cart physics under a lease (and the lease governs *who*, not *what*), or C10a takes on running Unity physics for vehicles server-side — a category of work C0-C8 has never done.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: The vanilla churn funnel actively fights a continuous lease
hazards.why: `ZDOMan.ReleaseNearbyZDOS` runs server-side every 2 s and releases/reseizes persistent ZDOs purely on active-area geometry, with no knowledge of `attachJoint` or `InUse()` (ZDOMan.cs:623-648). A lease for a cart must therefore either suppress this funnel for leased objects (the existing OwnershipPinRunner shape) or accept that the world can revoke the lease under the holder every 2 s. Note the difference from C4: an item pickup completes inside one interaction; a cart pull spans minutes of movement across zone boundaries — exactly the input that funnel keys on.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: There is no grant message to carry, and the client attaches by observing ownership
hazards.why: `Vagon.RPC_RequestOwn` grants by `SetOwner(sender)` with no reply (Vagon.cs:130-144); the requester attaches on the first FixedUpdate where `IsOwner()` is true (Vagon.cs:163-180). Only the DENY has a wire message. If Lumberjacks replaces the ZDO-owner change with a lease, the attach trigger disappears — `IsOwner()` will be whatever the redirected ZDO layer says, which may no longer correlate with holding the lease. The contract test has to pin down what makes the joint appear, and it cannot be 'the client noticed it became owner'.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Attach intent never expires; a lease epoch does
hazards.why: `m_useRequester` is cleared only inside the owner branch of FixedUpdate or by RPC_RequestDenied (Vagon.cs:146-153, 163-180). Combined with the unowned-cart broadcast (ZNetView.cs:326-329 + ZRoutedRpc.Everybody == 0), a press that goes nowhere leaves a live intent that fires whenever ownership eventually lands — including from the server's unrelated reseize. Under a lease with an epoch and an expiry, a stale intent can attach the cart against an expired or reissued lease. Vanilla's own 'cart didn't respond, then grabbed by itself' behaviour is this bug.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Losing the lease mid-pull silently detaches and re-arms friendly fire
hazards.why: The non-owner branch is one unconditional line — `else if (IsAttached()) { Detach(); }` (Vagon.cs:186-189) — so any lease revocation drops the joint that tick with no player-facing message, and `Attack` stops skipping the cart because the immunity test reads the local joint (Attack.cs:1249-1253, Vagon.cs:207-214). Lease reclaim/expiry policy for vehicles needs a defined UX and a grace window, or normal AoI movement will look like the cart 'dropping' and players will start chopping their own carts.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Stale `attachJoint = 1` marks a free cart as in-use, and persists into the save
hazards.why: `Detach` clears the ZDO flag only when `IsOwner()` (Vagon.cs:302-305), and `OnDestroy` clears nothing at all (Vagon.cs:101-104) even though `ZNetScene.RemoveObjects` destroys the object on active-area exit (ZNetScene.cs:305-316). Vanilla self-heals on the next owner's FixedUpdate; a Lumberjacks lease lane that derives 'is this vehicle in use' from the replicated flag inherits a field that is written by one side, cleared conditionally, never cleared on unload, and saved to disk in the true state.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Two ownership-transfer paths into the same ZDO, only one of which is the vehicle path
hazards.why: `Container.RPC_RequestOpen`/`RPC_RequestStack`/`RPC_RequestTakeAll` each do `ForceSendZDO(uid, …)` then `SetOwner(uid)` on the cart's ZNetView (Container.cs:293-294, 339-340, and the parallel take-all at :383-395), cross-guarded against `m_wagon.InUse()`. C10a's family-1 (vehicles) and family-2 (containers/duping) gates therefore collide on the cart: the same lease must cover both the pull and the inventory. Also note vanilla's ordering — state flush BEFORE handover — which any lease handoff should replicate or it will hand a new owner a stale inventory.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: `attachJoint` is an int on cart ZDOs and a string on character ZDOs
hazards.why: `ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash` (ZDOVars.cs:29) is written by Vagon via `Set(hash, bool)` → int table (ZDO.cs:381-384) and by ZSyncTransform via `Set(hash, string)` → string table (ZSyncTransform.cs:190, read at :289). Vanilla tolerates this because ZDOExtraData is type-partitioned and the two live on different ZDOs. A Lumberjacks ZDO journal or contract test that maps stable-hash → a single declared type will mis-decode one of them, and the failure mode is a cart that reads as permanently attached or a rider whose attach point decodes as garbage.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Riders create cross-ZDO transform connections that compete with C6 motion authority
hazards.why: A character standing in the cart writes `SetConnection(ConnectionType.SyncTransform, cartZdo)` plus relPos/relRot/relVel onto its OWN ZDO (Character.cs:3732-3753, ZSyncTransform.cs:183-214), and remote clients then position that character relative to the cart, invoking the cart's `ClientSync` re-entrantly and directly (ZSyncTransform.cs:281-291) — bypassing `CustomFixedUpdate`, which is where `MotionAuthorityTransformPatch` hooks (MotionAuthorityPatches.cs:11-17). So the C6 seam does not cover the parent-driven path. C6 established motion frames as the sole remote source of player transform; a rider's transform is by construction relative to a non-player entity, which is precisely the 'different in kind' the brief suspected — and it is real.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: The audit's `RPC_RequestOwn` = superseded row is not true for Vagon, and orphans `RPC_RequestDenied`
hazards.why: C8-BREADTH-AUDIT-2026-07-31.md:39 says the ArmorStand/ItemStand/Vagon registrants ride the replaced dance, but the only implemented patch is `[HarmonyPatch(nameof(ItemDrop.RequestOwn))]` (OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner.cs:1156-1158) — the ItemDrop caller method, not the shared RPC name, and nothing at all on Vagon. Meanwhile `RPC_RequestDenied` (Vagon.Awake, per synthetic_baseline_v2.json) sits in the 118-row needs-lane bucket: the reply is scheduled for admission while the request it replies to is marked superseded. C10a should re-open that single row rather than inherit an inconsistent pair.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Under the current native-zero composition carts are already broken, untested
hazards.why: `RpcRoutedRpcPrefix` poisons the inbound routed funnel wholesale (NativeNetworkPatches.cs:201-209) and the Lumberjacks admission dictionary holds seven method names (RoutedRpcCutoverRunner.cs:526-538), none of them Vagon's. By source, a poison-armed C8 build cannot deliver RPC_RequestOwn or RPC_RequestDenied. This is inferred, not observed — no cart was in any C8 scenario — but it means 'C8 native-zero passed' carries no signal about carts, and a first cart contract test should expect failure, not regression.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Unowned-cart interaction broadcasts to every peer
hazards.why: `InvokeRPC(method)` targets `m_zdo.GetOwner()` (ZNetView.cs:326-329); owner 0 equals `ZRoutedRpc.Everybody` (ZRoutedRpc.cs:41) and `RouteRPC` fans out to all ready peers (ZRoutedRpc.cs:146-164). Every cart is unowned immediately after a world load. A Lumberjacks lane must decide explicitly where an ownerless-vehicle request goes — the gateway is the natural answer, and it is strictly better than vanilla's broadcast-and-hope.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: The priority classifier bands a moving cart with chests
hazards.why: LumberjacksPriorityClassifier.cs:44 matches `"cart"` into `storage_crafting` at rank 4 — below structural anchors. A pulled cart needs transform updates at motion rates; a parked one does not, and a name-only rule cannot tell them apart. The band policy itself is distance-based (ZdoBandPolicy), so the interaction between the two needs checking before a cart test is meaningful.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Every cart stream-in forces a full heightmap regeneration
hazards.why: `Heightmap.ForceGenerateAll()` in `Vagon.Awake` (Vagon.cs:86). If Lumberjacks' AoI causes carts to enter/leave the active set more often than vanilla — plausible if the band policy drops and re-adds a rank-4 object as its distance oscillates — this becomes a repeated client hitch attributable to the new transport.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Non-owners write to the cart's physics and its ZDO with nothing stopping them
hazards.why: `Detach` runs `m_body.WakeUp(); m_body.AddForce(0f, 1f, 0f);` unguarded (Vagon.cs:306-307) and is reachable on non-owned carts via the static `DetachAll()` and the non-owner FixedUpdate branch. More broadly, `ZDO.Set(int, int, bool okForNotOwner = false)` never reads its own guard parameter (ZDO.cs:352-358) — vanilla has no ownership enforcement on field writes at all. A fail-closed lease design must add that enforcement rather than assume it exists.

hazards.lens: Carts (Vagon) — attach/detach, cart ZDO ownership, physics locus, and ownership churn, read from decompiled vanilla source and cross-checked against the Baseline mod's cutover seams
hazards.hazard: Puller extra-mass leaks on unload
hazards.why: `SetExtraMass` mutates the local Rigidbody mass directly (Character.cs:3885-3888) and is reverted only in `Detach`; `OnDestroy` does not call it (Vagon.cs:101-104). If `m_playerExtraPullMass` is non-zero on the prefab, a cart unloading while attached leaves the player permanently heavier until the next attach/detach cycle. Cosmetic in vanilla, but it is client-local state that diverges from anything the server believes.

hazards.hazard: OwnerRevision is a 16-bit counter compared with `>`
hazards.why: ZDOMan.cs:828 gates the owner apply on `num3 > zDO.OwnerRevision` where the revision is a `ushort` (ZDO.cs:203). Long sessions with heavy churn — carts being exactly the churn-heavy case — can wrap it, after which ownership updates stall on the stale branch. Worth a bound in the contract test rather than a fix.

hazards.lens: ZSyncTransform and non-player entity motion — how vehicle/creature transforms actually replicate in vanilla Valheim, and what carries them today under Baseline's Lumberjacks transport.
hazards.hazard: There is no server-side vehicle simulation to become authoritative over — this is greenfield, not a replacement
hazards.why: ZNet.m_referencePosition (ZNet.cs:163) is only ever set from local-player code (Player.cs:644/1502, Game.cs:459/488/510/513), so a headless server leaves it at Vector3.zero and ZNetScene (:202, :360-365) never instantiates a ship at sea. No GameObject means no Rigidbody, no buoyancy solver, no ZSyncTransform. Every previous slice replaced a native mechanism that existed on the server; a server-authoritative ship has nothing to replace and would require Baseline to stand up vehicle physics on the server from scratch (or accept designated-client authority and validate rather than simulate). This distinction should be settled before C10a scoping, because 'extend the C4 lease to vehicles' quietly assumes the server can adjudicate a position it cannot compute.

hazards.lens: ZSyncTransform and non-player entity motion — how vehicle/creature transforms actually replicate in vanilla Valheim, and what carries them today under Baseline's Lumberjacks transport.
hazards.hazard: The canonical motion frame cannot express a vehicle's orientation
hazards.why: ValheimMotionSnapshot (ValheimMotionCodec.cs:120-138) carries Yaw as a single float. Vanilla replicates full Euler rotation (ZDO.cs:471) plus body_avel angular velocity (ZSyncTransform.cs:239). A longship pitches and rolls on waves and a cart tips on slopes; a yaw-only frame renders both perfectly flat and loses the upside-down state that Ship.UpdateUpsideDmg (Ship.cs:422-437) uses to deal damage. Extending motion authority to vehicles requires a wider frame, not a wider enrolment predicate.

hazards.hazard: Continuous control has no lease-shaped handoff to extend — the only handoff is a one-frame snap with no epoch
hazards.why: ZSyncTransform.cs:129-151 is the entire vanilla control transfer: on the rising edge of ownership, reload transform + linear/angular velocity from the ZDO and Physics.SyncTransforms(). There is no epoch, expiry, reason or ack, and the C4 lease vocabulary has no counterpart for 'restore my rigidbody state at the moment I take the wheel'. A lease-based vehicle handoff that omits this restore will make a ship teleport or lurch on every control change; one that includes it must define whose velocity is canonical at the transfer instant. This is genuinely new protocol design, which is why the C8 audit's 'largest novel ownership work' label is right.

hazards.hazard: Three incompatible, unauthenticated ownership-transfer mechanisms will all be poisoned by a fail-closed lease lane
hazards.why: Ship.UpdateOwner (Ship.cs:690-699) unilaterally calls ZDO.SetOwner every 2 s to hand the boat to a passenger; Vagon.RPC_RequestOwn (Vagon.cs:130-144) does SetOwner(sender) on request; Sadle.RPC_RequestControl (Sadle.cs:339-356) does Set(s_user) AND SetOwner(sender) in one shot on the CREATURE's ZDO. The audit marks RPC_RequestOwn 'superseded (kept)' because ItemDrop.RequestOwn was replaced — but carts genuinely depend on it, and Ship's timer path is not an RPC at all, so an RPC-level poison will not catch it. Poisoning ownership writes without a vehicle lease first will strand ships with a departed owner and freeze carts mid-haul.

hazards.hazard: C6's player motion authority actively breaks the rider-on-vehicle case if naively extended
hazards.why: For a rider, the truth is parent-relative: connection ConnectionType.SyncTransform + relPos/relRot on the RIDER's ZDO, resolved in the parent's frame (ZSyncTransform.cs:276-341). C6 replaces the remote player's transform with a WORLD-space Lumberjacks frame (SuppressNativeTransform, LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:1369) and masks native ZDO position writes (:1384). A remote player standing on a moving deck would then be placed by a 5-30 Hz world-space frame instead of being pinned to the deck, so they will visibly slide, lag behind the hull, and interact with the C6 implausible-target guard (the code already treats >30 m jumps as needing the reliable resync lane, and a fast longship covers that in seconds). This is the concrete reason vehicles are 'different in kind' — it is not just a wider entity set, it is a different coordinate frame.

hazards.hazard: The parent-before-child in-frame ordering guarantee has no analogue in the Lumberjacks lane
hazards.why: ZSyncTransform.SyncPosition reaches into the parent and calls component.ClientSync(dt) directly (:287), protected by the m_lastUpdateFrame dedupe (:379-383), precisely so the vehicle's transform is final before the rider is placed on it. A Lumberjacks motion applier that processes entities in arbitrary order will place riders against a one-frame-stale hull, producing a persistent visual offset proportional to ship speed.

hazards.hazard: The native OWNER-side writer is entirely unpatched and will race any new vehicle authority
hazards.why: MotionAuthorityPatches.cs:11 patches only ZSyncTransform.CustomFixedUpdate. OwnerSync/CustomLateUpdate keeps writing SetPosition/SetRotation/vel/body_vel into every owned ZDO (ZSyncTransform.cs:169-242). The moment Lumberjacks starts asserting a vehicle transform, two writers exist for the same ZDO on the same machine and the last LateUpdate wins. The C6 pattern of a paired suppress-writer/mask-ZDO-write will need a vehicle-shaped equivalent, and ZDO.InternalSetPosition masking alone will not cover SetRotation or the body_vel hashes.

hazards.hazard: Suppressing ClientSync for a vehicle also silently re-enables its remote physics
hazards.why: ZSyncTransform.cs:430-452 is where a non-owner forces m_body.useGravity = false and either injects body_vel/body_avel or Sleep()s the body. A Harmony prefix that returns false on CustomFixedUpdate skips all of that. Every remote client's ship would then have gravity re-enabled with an awake, unconstrained Rigidbody — it would sink, drift, and fight the injected transform. The C6 player case survives this only because remote players are handled by other suppression; a vehicle replacement must explicitly own this side-effect.

hazards.hazard: 'vel' means two different things depending on parenting, and both meanings are on the wire today
hazards.why: OwnerSync writes world velocity into ZDOVars.s_velHash at :179 and then overwrites it with parent-relative velocity at :202 in the same pass when parented. The receiver reads it as relative at :292 and as world at :357, discriminated only by whether the SyncTransform connection resolves. Any Lumberjacks schema that types 'vel' as a single world-space vector is wrong for every rider, and the error is silent — it produces plausible-looking drift, not a crash.

hazards.hazard: Distance band shaping will visibly stutter a moving vehicle
hazards.why: ZdoRedirectRunner.IsPlayerCharacterZdo (:664-681) matches only peer character ZDOIDs, so ships and carts get no fast lane. Defaults (PluginConfig.cs:797-825) thin 30-64 m to 5 Hz and DROP beyond 64 m. A longship at full sail crosses a 64 m band in a few seconds, so an observer watching a boat sail past sees it thinned then dropped, relying entirely on ZSyncTransform's 2 s dead-reckoning (:311) to paper over it. A vehicle fast lane, or a velocity-aware band, is a prerequisite for any honest vehicle acceptance test.

hazards.hazard: Motion smoothing is coupled to unrelated ZDO writes through DataRevision
hazards.why: m_posRevision compares zdo.DataRevision (ZSyncTransform.cs:294, :348) and resets the extrapolation timer on ANY change. A ship writes 'forward' and 'rudder' from UpdateControlls every FixedUpdate (Ship.cs:571-572) on the same ZDO. If those writes bump DataRevision, the receiver's extrapolation clock resets ~50x/second and dead reckoning is effectively disabled for ships; if a Lumberjacks lane synthesizes DataRevision differently than native, it changes the visible smoothing behaviour without touching any motion code.

hazards.hazard: Vehicle control RPCs are unauthenticated even against the vehicle's own user field
hazards.why: Ship's RPC_Rudder/RPC_Forward/RPC_Backward/RPC_Stop (Ship.cs:242-297) never check the sender against ShipControlls' s_user, and never check IsOwner. Sadle.RPC_Controls at least checks IsOwner (:274). Any lane that routes these RPCs through Lumberjacks inherits an authorization hole that C4's lease vocabulary is well positioned to close — but that means the lease must gate a CONTINUOUS RPC stream (rudder every 0.2 s, Controls every input frame), not a one-shot mutating action, which is a different validation shape than the C4 pickup proof.

hazards.hazard: Vagon attachment state is not replicated at all — only a bool is
hazards.why: AttachTo builds a local Unity ConfigurableJoint (Vagon.cs:252-285) and publishes only a bool under 'attachJoint'. Non-owners destroy their joint every FixedUpdate (:186-189). A cart's physical coupling to the player exists on exactly one machine. Any Baseline model that treats 'who is pulling this cart' as replicated state is modelling something vanilla does not have.

hazards.hazard: Vagon writes ZDOVars.s_attachJointHash as a bool while ZSyncTransform writes it as a string
hazards.why: Vagon.cs:279 does Set(s_attachJointHash, value: true) (int-backed); ZSyncTransform.cs:190 does Set(s_attachJointHash, string). Separate ZDOExtraData type tables mean no runtime collision, but a Lumberjacks ZDO field schema keyed on the hash name will mistype one of them. Worth a contract test in C10a rather than a runtime surprise.

hazards.lens: Rider and passenger transform relationship — how an attached player is positioned locally and replicated, and what Baseline's motion authority does to it
hazards.hazard: Attachment is invisible on the Lumberjacks wire, and the code that would have used it is switched off
hazards.why: The 36-byte motion payload (ValheimMotionCodec.cs:43-54) has no parent ZDOID, no attach-joint string, and no relative pose. Independently, the Harmony prefix on ZSyncTransform.CustomFixedUpdate (MotionAuthorityPatches.cs:11-16) deletes the ENTIRE reconstruction path for a canonical remote — connection lookup, parent-first ClientSync ordering, TransformPoint(relPos), the mount bone snap, and relative-velocity extrapolation. Even if native ZDO replication still delivered relPos, no observer would read it. C10a cannot treat vehicles as an RPC-admission problem: the motion contract itself needs a parent/attachment channel, or a separate attachment lane that the observer consults before applying a world-space frame.

hazards.lens: Rider and passenger transform relationship — how an attached player is positioned locally and replicated, and what Baseline's motion authority does to it
hazards.hazard: A freshness hold strands a rider in world space while the vehicle sails out from under them, with no native recovery
hazards.why: On a stale sample the authority path calls HoldRemote (LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:207, 1425-1431), which zeroes velocity and sets a reason but does NOT clear HasAppliedPosition. Since HasRemote (line 1419) gates suppression on that flag, native ZSyncTransform stays suppressed throughout the hold. Default lumberjacksMotionFreshSeconds is 0.5 s (PluginConfig.cs:545). Under native relative sync a stale rider stays glued to the deck because relPos is constant; under Baseline the rider freezes at a world point and the ship leaves. Fail-closed is the right policy for a walking player and the wrong policy for an attached one, because the correct hold behaviour is 'hold in the vehicle frame', which Baseline has no representation of.

hazards.lens: Rider and passenger transform relationship — how an attached player is positioned locally and replicated, and what Baseline's motion authority does to it
hazards.hazard: Positional error scales with vehicle speed, where native error was structurally zero
hazards.why: Native relative sync makes a seated rider's tangential error zero by construction, and gives the mount case an exact per-FixedUpdate bone snap with no interpolation (ZSyncTransform.cs:299-306). Baseline's error is (one-way network latency + the ~56 ms smoothing time constant from lumberjacksMotionSmoothing=18, LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:198) multiplied by vehicle speed, plus up to one 20 Hz send interval. At longship speeds that is metres of visible aft-slide — a passenger apparently standing in the sea, or a rider bobbing behind a running Lox. This is a quality regression that will not show up in any on-foot A/B.

hazards.hazard: The 30 m implausible-target guard is a speed-dependent tripwire that raises authority_failures, not just a visual glitch
hazards.why: ImplausibleTargetMeters is a hard 30.0 f (LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:35) applied to |current - target| on the ordinary lane; exceeding it calls HoldRemote AND increments _authorityFailures (lines 312-322), which fails the probe gates outright (EvaluateProbe requires failures == 0, lines 955-985). Combined with the 0.5 s freshness window, any stall on a moving vehicle can present a resumed target beyond the bound, converting a routine packet gap into a recorded authority failure. The bound was calibrated for on-foot speeds; the sender-side teleport-resync detector (line 607-612) uses the same 30 m constant between consecutive 20 Hz samples and will not fire for legitimate vehicle motion, so nothing re-anchors the rider.

hazards.hazard: A lagging remote passenger can fall out of the ship's trigger volume on the OWNER's client and stop the boat or deny the helm
hazards.why: Ship.m_players is built from local OnTriggerEnter/OnTriggerExit against the rendered collider (Ship.cs:730-766) — i.e. against whatever position Baseline wrote. On the ship's ZDO owner, that list gates real behaviour: m_players.Count == 0 forces Speed.Stop and zeroes the rudder (Ship.cs:311-315), CanBeRemoved() becomes true (Ship.cs:181), and ShipControlls.RPC_RequestControl refuses the helm unless IsPlayerInBoat(playerID) on that same owner (ShipControlls.cs:95). Baseline's world-space placement is exactly the input to those triggers, so presentation lag becomes a gameplay-state fault on a machine that is not the lagging player's.

hazards.lens: Rider and passenger transform relationship — how an attached player is positioned locally and replicated, and what Baseline's motion authority does to it
hazards.hazard: Rotation is yaw-only, so riders cannot tilt with a rolling deck or a moving mount
hazards.why: Baseline forces Quaternion.Euler(0, yaw, 0) (LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:334) and the wire carries yaw as a uint16 at 0.1-degree resolution (ValheimMotionCodec.cs:51). Native reconstructs the attached rotation as parentRotation * relRot — a full quaternion (ZSyncTransform.cs:334) — and Player.UpdateAttach copies the attach point's full rotation locally (Player.cs:5987). Remote riders will be gimbal-upright on a pitching longship and misaligned in a saddle, intersecting hull and mount geometry. Note this also means the rider's own client and every observer disagree about the rider's orientation, which matters for any future hit/aim work.

hazards.lens: Rider and passenger transform relationship — how an attached player is positioned locally and replicated, and what Baseline's motion authority does to it
hazards.hazard: Non-owner rigidbody gravity and sleep management lived inside the method the prefix skips
hazards.why: m_body.useGravity = false, m_body.Sleep(), and the velocity assignment for non-owned bodies are all inside ZSyncTransform.ClientSync (lines 430-453), reachable only through the suppressed CustomFixedUpdate. Baseline writes body.linearVelocity in LateUpdate (lines 338-344) but never disables gravity and never calls Physics.SyncTransforms() after writing transform.position — native calls it after every write (lines 338-341, 364-367). For a walking remote this is masked by a per-frame position rewrite; for an attached rider whose target is a moving frame it compounds with the lag. I did not find another site that disables gravity on remote player bodies, but I could not prove absence — see open questions.

hazards.hazard: Vagon does not fit a vehicle-lease abstraction copied from Ship/Sadle
hazards.why: The cart has no player attachment, no attach point on the player, no relative transform, and no control seat. It is a local ConfigurableJoint that exists only on the cart's owner and is torn down by every non-owner (Vagon.cs:186-189, 252-285), coordinated by the pre-lease RPC_RequestOwn (line 130). The C8 audit already lists RPC_RequestOwn as 'superseded' by the C4 lease, which is right for the ownership handshake but says nothing about the joint. A single 'vehicle control lease' shape modelled on Ship/Sadle will silently mis-describe the cart, and the cart's pull force on the player also mutates the player's own mass (SetExtraMass, line 283).

hazards.hazard: Scope is 'anyone aboard', not 'anyone in a control seat'
hazards.why: Base Character.GetRelativePosition (Character.cs:3732-3746) parents any character standing on a ZNetView-bearing rigidbody, with a real relative velocity term. So an unseated deckhand walking a longship, and any tamed creature or enemy standing on it, are relatively synced natively. Sizing C10a's vehicle work around RequestControl/ReleaseControl (the two [VERIFY] rows named in the C8 audit) will undercount the surface by the whole passenger and cargo-creature population.

hazards.hazard: No existing ZDO field names which player is attached to which seat, so the attachment channel must invent that identity
hazards.why: The only replicated traces of attachment are the SyncTransform connection plus relPos/relRot/attachJoint (all written by ZSyncTransform, which Baseline neither writes nor reads), the s_inBed bool set in AttachStart (Player.cs:5961), the attach animation bool on ZSyncAnimation, and s_user on the vehicle. There is no chair-occupancy field at all — Chair.Interact does a purely local GetClosestPlayer proximity check (Chair.cs:56-61). A Lumberjacks attachment lane cannot mirror an existing field; it has to define seat identity from scratch, which is a contract-design task, not a port.

hazards.lens: Baseline lease model and its assumptions — the C4 ownership-lease contract as actually built (Gateway ValheimOwnershipLeaseService + mod OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner + MessageRouter), and which of its assumptions a continuous-control object (ship/cart/mount) violates.
hazards.hazard: The authorization gate is a one-shot latch — a continuous-control lease has no shape in the built model
hazards.why: OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner.cs:426 throws if `target.Completed || target.Authorized`, and the Gateway marks the slot `completed` on the first result (ValheimOwnershipLeaseService.cs:102-104). A helm lease that authorizes rudder input for the duration of a voyage cannot be expressed by extending C4; it needs a second lifecycle state ('held/streaming') that no code, contract or test currently has. This is the difference-in-kind the C8 audit suspected, and it is confirmed in source.

hazards.hazard: Maximum lease lifetime is 30 seconds, hard-thrown at the Gateway
hazards.why: ValheimOwnershipLeaseService.cs:24 rejects any duration > 30 s. A crossing, a cart haul or a ride is minutes. Sustained control therefore requires renewal at ≥2/minute per vehicle per rider, and the only renewal verb is `reissue` — a full client→Gateway→game-server→Gateway→client round trip (MessageRouter.cs:1230-1414) that mints a NEW epoch, invalidating every action frame already in flight under the old one (Validate requires exact epoch equality, line 61). Renewal is a stop-the-world event, not a heartbeat.

hazards.hazard: There is no lease-request verb for a pre-existing world object
hazards.why: phase=='create' requires uid_user/uid_id == 0 (MessageRouter.cs:1257-1259) and the game server responds by INSTANTIATING the target (OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner.cs:352-359); phase=='reissue' requires the uid to match the object that same action created (lines 383-390). 'Give me control of that longship' has no message in the protocol. Every C4 gate ran against an object the lease command spawned, so the admission path for an arbitrary existing ZDO is entirely unbuilt — not merely unproven.

hazards.hazard: Reclaim-on-disconnect is blanket and terminal, and the game server is never told
hazards.why: GameWebSocketMiddleware.cs:296-299 reclaims all of a peer's active leases on ANY socket loss, ahead of the 2-minute resume window the transport otherwise honours, and emits no frame to the logical server. Mid-voyage a 3-second WebSocket blip therefore (a) strips helm authority with no notification to the helmsman, (b) leaves the vehicle's native ZDO owner wherever the last authorized action put it, and (c) leaves nobody designated to simulate the boat's physics. For C4's 0.75 s ownership blip this divergence was invisible; for a vehicle it is the central failure mode.

hazards.hazard: No handoff / transfer verb — contention is rejection-only
hazards.why: The 'contend' phase (MessageRouter.cs:1274-1305) answers a second peer with holder_mismatch and never mutates the lease; the only route from holder A to holder B is A's lease dying then B obtaining a fresh Issue. Vanilla ships do the opposite: Ship.UpdateOwner (Ship.cs:690-699) reassigns ownership peer-to-peer every 2 s when the owner leaves the boat, and Sadle.RPC_RequestControl (Sadle.cs:349) transfers ownership as part of granting control. Passing the helm, or an owner walking off a moving boat, is exactly the case with no lease-model expression.

hazards.hazard: The frame budget does not survive vehicle cadence
hazards.why: One lease+action cycle is ~10 reliable frames (request, command, issue, granted, receipt, action, authorized, result, completed, result-receipt) plus per-frame ACKs, all on the single ordered per-connection reliable lane (MessageClassification.cs:29-46), against a 256-frame window on both sides. Vanilla control cadence is 5 Hz for the ship rudder (Ship.cs:218) and per-input-frame for Sadle 'Controls' (Sadle.cs:268 via Player.cs:6182). Even at one lease-validated action per rudder tick that is ~50 reliable frames/s/rider before any ZDO journal traffic. Wall 14 already proved this lane starvable at exactly 256 with a benign interest re-publish; a vehicle would be the flood, not the victim.

hazards.hazard: The Gateway's outbound reliable window has no control-frame bypass, and a refusal throws
hazards.why: Wall 14's fix (LumberjacksGameSessionRunner.cs:1178-1186) force-enqueues ownership frames on the MOD side only. ReliableGameSessionState.TryEnqueue (SessionManager.cs:338-346) has no `force`, and every ownership SendReliableAsync in MessageRouter throws InvalidOperationException on `!Queued` (e.g. lines 1394-1395, 1484-1485). A grant or authorization to a busy holder can still be refused with reliable_send_queue_full — and the refusal takes down the connection rather than degrading. The half of wall 14 that faces the client is unfixed.

hazards.hazard: Exactly one in-flight lease per client, and exactly one lease slot per object
hazards.why: OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner.cs:92 refuses a second concurrent probe, and the Gateway key is one lease per object (line 137). A vehicle scene is inherently multi-object and multi-authority: the cart plus the ox pulling it (Vagon.cs:130-144 has its own RPC_RequestOwn → SetOwner dance), the helm plus each passenger's attachment, the mount plus its MonsterAI. The model has no notion of a correlated lease set, and no notion of two peers holding non-conflicting rights over the same vehicle.

hazards.hazard: Rider-relative transform has no carriage in any replacement lane
hazards.why: ZSyncTransform's characterParentSync writes a ConnectionType.SyncTransform connection plus s_relPos/s_relRot/s_vel into the RIDER's ZDO (ZSyncTransform.cs:183-207), and Player.UpdateAttach slaves the rider's world transform to the attach point every frame (Player.cs:5980-5999). C6's motion lane is player-world-position only and masks player-ZDO position writes (LumberjacksMotionRunner.cs:1384-1398); the journal carries only ConnectionType.Portal at runtime (ZdoJournalCutoverRunner.cs:680). So a passenger on a moving boat is currently a player whose canonical world position is being authored by a motion lane that knows nothing about the deck they are standing on.

hazards.hazard: Nothing designates who simulates a non-player rigidbody
hazards.why: C6 established sole remote authority for PLAYER transforms; the lease established a 0.75 s ownership blip for a one-shot mutation. Neither answers 'whose machine runs the boat's physics for the next four minutes, and what happens the instant that machine stops answering'. Vanilla answers it with ZDO ownership (Ship.CustomFixedUpdate early-returns on !IsOwner, Ship.cs:305-308), which is precisely the mechanism the cutover is replacing.

hazards.hazard: Fail-closed-by-throw is the wrong failure mode for a control stream
hazards.why: Both ends treat contract violations as fatal: the mod throws InvalidDataException out of Update on any invariant miss (e.g. OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner.cs:301, 331, 492, 621) and the router throws on malformed or non-'pickup' actions. That is correct for an unattended probe that must not silently degrade. Applied to a 5–60 Hz control stream, one stale-epoch frame arriving after a reissue — a normal race, not a defect — terminates the runner or the connection.

hazards.hazard: The result contract cannot express a failed action, and its payload is inventory-shaped
hazards.why: MessageRouter.cs:1508 throws when success is false, and the completion payload is item_prefab + item_count 1..100, re-checked on the client against `payload.item_count != 1` and the Raspberry prefab (OwnershipLeaseCutoverRunner.cs:611-621). Vehicle control outcomes ('rudder applied', 'out of stamina', 'collision, control lost') have neither a success-shape nor a failure-shape here.

hazards.hazard: Unbounded per-session state under repeated lease traffic
hazards.why: _leases is never pruned (ValheimOwnershipLeaseService.cs:11 — no Remove anywhere in the file) and _acceptedClientMessages accumulates one idempotency key per accepted reliable client message forever (SessionManager.cs:296, 387). At C4's handful of leases per run this is free; at a renewal every ≤30 s per vehicle per player across a long session it is a monotonic leak in a process whose restart is the documented fail-closed reset for all authority.
